rw: Materials management is the function that orders, stores and distributes the supplies and equipment a hospital needs, so wards and clinics have what they require when they need it to deliver care safely.

ww.Managing patient charts for the wards an: Patient charts are handled by health information management, which keeps records. Materials management deals with physical supplies and equipment, so records work does not fit this role at all.
ww.Managing meals only, for the patients an: Meals belong to dietary or nutrition services. Materials management covers all the supplies and equipment a hospital needs, far more than food, so limiting it to meals is incorrect.
ww.Managing staff schedules for nurses and: Scheduling nurses and doctors is a human resources and nursing administration task. Materials management is about physical goods moving through the hospital, not about people, shifts or staffing.

rw: A par level is the minimum quantity of an item to keep on hand, set so that when stock falls to it, staff reorder before the supply runs out.

ww.The golf score of a nurse who plays on w: Golf has nothing to do with supply management. A par level is an inventory threshold for stock, and this option borrows the word par from golf as a joke, which is wrong.
ww.The price of an item as shown in the sup: A catalog price is just a listed cost. A par level measures quantity of stock on hand, not money, so describing it as a price confuses inventory control with pricing.
ww.The maximum price that a hospital will p: A par level is about quantity, not a price ceiling. It is the minimum stock that triggers reordering, so a maximum price paid to a supplier describes a purchasing limit instead.

rw: A GPO is an entity that negotiates lower prices with suppliers on behalf of many member hospitals, using their combined buying volume to gain discounts that a single hospital could not get alone.

ww.A group of patients who share a ward and: Patients who share a ward are not a purchasing group. A GPO is about buying supplies together to get lower prices, and has no link to patient care discussions or wards.
ww.A group of insurers that share risk and: Insurers that pool risk and pay claims describe a health plan or risk pool. A GPO does not pay claims; it negotiates supply prices for hospitals, so this describes the wrong industry.
ww.A group of doctors who share a clinic an: Doctors who share a clinic and split profits form a medical group practice. A GPO is a purchasing body for hospital supplies, so a profit sharing doctors group is the wrong thing entirely.

rw: CLIA, the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, is the federal program that sets quality standards for clinical laboratory testing, so results from labs are accurate, reliable and timely for patient care.

ww.A program for hospital food that sets th: Hospital food rules come from nutrition and food safety standards, not from CLIA. CLIA applies to laboratory testing, so a program for meals served to patients is not what it covers.
ww.A program for drug pricing that sets the: Drug prices are not set by CLIA. Pharmacy pricing is a matter of markets, insurers and manufacturers, while CLIA regulates the quality of clinical laboratory testing on human specimens.
ww.A program for nurse licensing that sets: Nurse licensing and exams are handled by state boards of nursing. CLIA is a federal laboratory program, so it has no role in setting rules for becoming a nurse.

rw: Environmental services, or housekeeping, cleans and disinfects patient rooms and other areas, which removes germs and helps prevent infection from spreading among patients, visitors and staff in the hospital.

ww.Treats patients who have broken bones an: Treating broken bones and injuries is done by physicians, orthopedic staff and emergency teams. Environmental services staff clean the facility, and they do not give medical treatment to patients.
ww.Prescribes drugs to patients after an ex: Prescribing drugs requires a license held by physicians and certain other providers after examining a patient. Housekeeping staff clean rooms and have no authority to prescribe medicine to anyone.
ww.Bills insurers for the care that was giv: Billing insurers is the work of the billing and revenue cycle office. Environmental services is the cleaning team, so sending bills for care is not part of its duties.

rw: Dietary or nutrition services plans and prepares meals that meet each patient's dietary needs, such as low salt or diabetic diets, which supports healing and keeps patients safe from foods that could harm them.

ww.Performs surgery on patients in the oper: Surgery is done by surgeons and operating room teams. Dietary services plan and prepare meals, so performing operations is far outside what this department does in a hospital.
ww.Handles billing of patients and insurers: Billing patients and insurers belongs to patient financial services or the billing office. Dietary services deals with food and nutrition, so handling bills is not among its tasks.
ww.Collects blood from patients for the lab: Collecting blood is done by phlebotomists or lab staff for testing. Dietary services works with food and nutrition, so drawing blood from patients is not part of that role.

rw: A respiratory therapist helps patients with breathing problems, including managing ventilators and giving oxygen, which is why this option fits the role and matches the lung and airway focus of the job.

ww.Processes claims for the care that was g: Processing claims is work done by billing and coding staff. A respiratory therapist treats breathing problems directly with patients, so claims handling is not part of the job.
ww.Prepares food for the patients and the s: Preparing food for patients and staff is done by dietary and cafeteria workers. Respiratory therapists focus on lungs and breathing, so cooking is not a duty they carry out.
ww.Fixes computers and the networks that li: Fixing computers and networks is done by information technology staff. A respiratory therapist works with patients who struggle to breathe, so repairing a network is outside this clinical role.

rw: A physical therapist helps patients restore movement and manage pain through exercise, stretching and other treatment, such as after surgery or injury, which is the defining purpose of this profession.

ww.Performs lab tests on blood and tissue s: Lab tests on blood and tissue samples are performed by laboratory technologists. Physical therapists work with movement and exercise, so analyzing samples in a lab is not their job.
ww.Does billing for the care that was given: Billing insurers for care is handled by the billing department. A physical therapist treats patients directly with exercise and movement therapy, so sending bills is not part of the role.
ww.Prescribes drugs to patients after an ex: Prescribing drugs after examining symptoms is done by physicians and other licensed prescribers. Physical therapists use exercise and manual therapy, and they do not prescribe drugs as a normal duty.

rw: Occupational therapists help patients regain the skills needed for daily living and work, such as dressing, cooking and using tools, after an illness, injury or disability has made these tasks hard.

ww.Treats only job injuries by surgery in o: Occupational therapists do not mainly treat job injuries by surgery. Surgeons operate, while occupational therapists use training and activities to help patients function, so this option confuses therapy with an operation.
ww.Sells equipment to patients who need aid: Selling equipment is a sales or supply role. Occupational therapists may recommend aids for home use, but their main job is helping patients regain skills, not selling goods.
ww.Finds jobs for patients who have left th: Finding jobs for discharged patients is a career or vocational placement service. Occupational therapy focuses on rebuilding the skills for tasks, not on locating employers or arranging employment for people.

rw: A hospital social worker helps patients and families find resources, plan for discharge and cope with illness, loss and stress, so this option correctly describes the support role they fill every day.

ww.Performs surgery on patients in the oper: Surgery is done by surgeons in operating rooms. A hospital social worker supports patients and families with resources and planning, and does not perform operations on anyone in the hospital.
ww.Prepares meals for the patients and the: Preparing meals is done by dietary and cafeteria staff. A social worker supports patients and families through counseling and planning, so cooking food for the hospital is not part of the job.
ww.Cleans rooms and halls in the wards of t: Cleaning rooms and halls is the work of environmental services staff. Social workers support patients and families with resources and coping, so cleaning is not within their job description.

rw: A health information manager oversees the quality, security and accessibility of patient health records, so that the data is accurate, protected from misuse and available to the people who need it for care.

ww.The hospital cafeteria and the food that: The cafeteria and its food are run by dietary or food service managers. A health information manager oversees patient records, so running a cafeteria falls outside that responsibility.
ww.The parking lot and the garages used by: Parking lots and garages are managed by facilities or security. A health information manager handles patient records and data, so oversight of parking has nothing to do with that function.
ww.The gift shop where visitors can buy car: The gift shop is run by volunteers or retail staff. A health information manager protects and manages health records, so overseeing the sale of cards and flowers is not the role.

rw: A medical coder translates medical documentation, such as diagnoses and procedures, into standard codes used for billing and for data, so insurers can pay claims and the hospital can report its statistics.

ww.Treats patients who are very sick and ne: Treating very sick patients who need constant watching is done by nurses and physicians in critical care. A medical coder works with records and codes, not with direct patient treatment on wards.
ww.Writes computer programs for the systems: Writing computer programs is the work of software developers or IT staff. A medical coder assigns codes to diagnoses and procedures from records, and does not program the hospital systems.
ww.Prepares food for the patients and for t: Preparing food is a job for dietary and cafeteria staff. Medical coders work at a desk turning documentation into codes, so cooking meals for patients and staff is not part of it.

rw: A patient access representative registers patients, verifies their insurance and collects the information needed at admission, which sets up the account and records so care and billing can follow smoothly afterward.

ww.Cleans rooms and halls of the wards in t: Cleaning rooms and halls of the wards is the work of environmental services staff. A patient access representative works at registration, so cleaning after each shift is not part of the job.
ww.Performs tests on blood and other sample: Performing tests on blood and other samples is done by laboratory staff. A patient access representative handles registration and insurance, so running tests on patient samples is not a duty of the role.
ww.Prepares medicines for the patients on t: Preparing medicines for the wards is done by pharmacists and pharmacy technicians. A patient access representative works on registration and insurance, and has no part in preparing or giving drugs.

rw: The Medicare Conditions of Participation are the federal health and safety standards hospitals must meet in order to take part in Medicare and be paid for care of Medicare patients.

ww.Rules for staff uniforms that tell nurse: Staff uniform rules are an internal hospital policy matter. The Medicare Conditions of Participation are federal health and safety standards for hospitals, and do not simply tell nurses and doctors what to wear.
ww.Rules for patients' diets that set the m: Patient diets are set by dietitians and physicians for each case. The Conditions of Participation are broad federal standards a hospital must meet for Medicare, not a rule set for what foods are served.
ww.Rules for parking that tell visitors and: Parking rules are a local facility matter. The Medicare Conditions of Participation are federal health and safety requirements for hospitals, and they do not cover where visitors and staff leave their cars.

rw: National Patient Safety Goals are Joint Commission requirements designed to prevent common patient safety problems, such as patient misidentification, medication errors and infections, and accredited hospitals are expected to follow them.

ww.Goals for hospital profits that set the: Profit targets for wards are a financial management matter. National Patient Safety Goals come from the Joint Commission and aim to prevent safety problems, not to set earnings for any ward.
ww.Goals for visitor numbers that set how m: Visitor numbers per ward are set by hospital visiting policy. National Patient Safety Goals address patient safety problems such as identification errors and infections, so they do not limit how many people may visit.
ww.Goals for staff hiring that set how many: Staff hiring numbers are a human resources decision. National Patient Safety Goals focus on preventing harm to patients, and do not tell a hospital how many people it must recruit.

rw: Using two identifiers, such as name and birth date, confirms the right patient receives the right treatment, which prevents medication errors and mix-ups between patients with similar names or conditions.

ww.To save time when a ward is busy and man: Using two identifiers is not about saving time. It adds a small step on purpose, because patient safety matters more than speed, even when a ward is busy and many patients wait.
ww.To collect data for sale to advertisers: Data for sale to advertisers is not a purpose of identifiers and would violate patient privacy rules. The two identifiers exist to protect patients from wrong treatment, not to build lists.
ww.To satisfy visitors who ask staff about: Satisfying visitors is not the reason. Visitors have no role in the check, and patient information is private. The identifiers are used to protect patients from receiving the wrong drug or treatment.

rw: A hospital-acquired infection is one a patient develops during a hospital stay that was not present on admission, which is how it differs from infections the patient brought with them when they arrived.

ww.An infection in computers, such as a vir: Computer viruses are not infections of people. A hospital-acquired infection is a medical condition caught by a patient in the hospital, so a virus on the network is the wrong meaning.
ww.An infection a patient has when arriving: An infection present on arrival is a community-acquired infection, recorded at admission. A hospital-acquired infection is one that was not there at admission, so this option describes the opposite case.
ww.An infection spread among staff only, wi: An infection limited to staff is an occupational illness. A hospital-acquired infection is defined by patients developing an infection during their stay, so excluding all patients makes this definition incorrect.

rw: Hand hygiene, which means washing with soap and water or using an alcohol rub, removes or kills germs on the hands and is the single most effective way to stop infection spreading.

ww.Shaking hands: Shaking hands passes germs from one person to another on the skin, so it spreads infection rather than preventing it. Hand hygiene breaks the chain of transmission and is the best defense.
ww.Wearing jewelry: Wearing jewelry can trap germs under rings and bracelets and makes hands harder to clean well, so it increases infection risk. It does not prevent the spread of infection among patients.
ww.Closed doors: Closed doors may limit airflow or noise, but they do not remove germs from hands, which are the main route of spread. Hand hygiene is far more effective at preventing infection.

rw: CLABSI is a serious bloodstream infection linked to a central venous catheter, a tube placed in a large vein, and hospitals work to prevent it with strict insertion and care procedures.

ww.A blood donation event held at the hospi: A blood donation event is a drive that collects blood. CLABSI is an infection linked to a central line, so the name refers to infection, not to giving blood.
ww.A fall in blood pressure after a loss of: A fall in blood pressure after blood loss is called hypotension or shock. CLABSI stands for central line-associated bloodstream infection, which is a germ infection in the blood and not low pressure.
ww.A broken IV pump that stops the flow of: A broken IV pump is an equipment failure. CLABSI is an infection of the bloodstream tied to a central line, so a machine fault that stops fluids is not what the term means.

rw: A never event is a serious, largely preventable error that should never happen, such as surgery on the wrong body part, and it signals a major failure in safety systems and procedures.

ww.A meeting that gets canceled because too: A canceled meeting is an ordinary scheduling matter. A never event is a serious patient safety error that is largely preventable, not a meeting that fails because too few staff can attend.
ww.An event that never starts because the s: An event that never starts because staff do not show up is a scheduling problem. A never event is a serious preventable error in care, such as a wrong-site operation.
ww.A holiday on which the hospital is close: A closure holiday is a normal operating decision. Never events are serious, largely preventable errors in patient care, so a day when the hospital is shut for patients and staff is not one.

rw: A near miss is an error or unsafe situation that was caught before it reached the patient, so no harm occurred, but it shows where a process could fail another time.

ww.A mistake that harmed a patient and was: A mistake that harmed a patient and was reported is an adverse event. A near miss is an error that did not reach the patient, so it cannot have caused harm.
ww.A canceled visit that a patient did not: A canceled visit that a patient skipped is a no-show. A near miss relates to safety errors that were caught in time, and has nothing to do with attendance at visits.
ww.A late bill that was sent to the patient: A late bill sent after the due date is an administrative problem. A near miss is a safety event caught before reaching a patient, so billing delays are not an example.

rw: Near misses reveal weaknesses in processes and systems, so the hospital can fix them and prevent harm before an error reaches a patient, which is the main reason they should be reported.

ww.To blame staff for each error that is re: Reporting is meant to improve systems, not to blame staff. Blame discourages reporting, so a culture of safety treats near misses as chances to learn rather than to punish people.
ww.To raise costs for the hospital through: Reporting is not meant to raise hospital costs. Near miss reports help prevent harm and the costs of real errors, so the benefit outweighs the small amount of paperwork involved in reporting.
ww.To avoid training of staff on the wards: Reporting does not avoid training. Near misses often show where staff need more training or better processes, so the reports lead to more learning on wards and in clinics, not less.

rw: A culture of safety is an environment where staff report problems freely, without fear of blame, and learn from them so that care improves and patients are better protected from harm.

ww.A museum of safety tools that shows old: A museum of old gear is a display of history. A culture of safety is a set of shared values and habits in a workplace, not a place that shows early hospital tools.
ww.A ban on reporting, so that staff never: A ban on reporting is the opposite of a culture of safety. Such a culture encourages staff to speak up about problems and risks so that they can be fixed.
ww.A rule to hide errors from the managers: Hiding errors from managers, patients and families is the opposite of a safety culture. Openness and honest reporting are needed so that errors can be understood, corrected and prevented in future.

rw: Medication reconciliation compares a patient's medication lists at transitions of care, such as admission, transfer and discharge, to find omissions, duplicates and conflicts so that medication errors can be avoided.

ww.To bill insurers for the drugs that were: Billing insurers for drugs given is a finance task. Medication reconciliation is a safety process that compares medication lists, so it has no purpose related to charging insurers for drugs.
ww.To order new drugs for the pharmacy shel: Ordering drugs for the pharmacy shelves is inventory work. Medication reconciliation compares what a patient is taking across care settings to avoid mistakes, and does not restock the pharmacy when stock runs low.
ww.To count pills for sale in shops, by sta: Counting pills for sale in shops is a retail pharmacy task. Medication reconciliation is a patient safety process that checks a patient's medication lists, not a way to count stock for sale.

rw: The five rights of medication administration are the right patient, right drug, right dose, right route and right time, and checking all five before giving a drug helps prevent medication errors.

ww.Right color, shape, size, smell and tast: Color, shape, size, smell and taste are traits of a pill, and they are not the five rights. Checking appearance alone does not confirm the right patient, drug, dose, route and time.
ww.Right doctor, nurse, aide, clerk and gua: Doctor, nurse, aide, clerk and guard are job roles in the hospital. The five rights check the details of a medication order, not the people who work in the building.
ww.Right price, brand, store, bag and recei: Price, brand, store, bag and receipt are shopping details. The five rights of medication administration are the right patient, drug, dose, route and time, which protect patients from errors, not buyers.

rw: An institutional review board reviews research involving people in order to protect participants' rights and welfare, checking that risks are reasonable, consent is informed and the study is ethical.

ww.To review staff schedules and the shifts: Staff schedules and nurses' shifts are managed by nursing administration. An institutional review board reviews research involving people, so it does not review work schedules of any ward.
ww.To review hospital menus and the meals s: Hospital menus are the concern of dietary services. An IRB protects people who take part in research, so reviewing meals served to patients is not its role.
ww.To review parking for staff and visitors: Parking is a facilities matter. An IRB exists to protect research participants, so reviewing the number of parking spaces for staff and visitors has nothing to do with its purpose.

rw: The minimum necessary standard under HIPAA means using or sharing only the least amount of protected health information needed for a given purpose, which limits exposure of private patient data.

ww.The minimum wage that a hospital must pa: Minimum wage is a labor law matter. The HIPAA minimum necessary standard is about limiting the use and sharing of protected health information, and has no connection with pay for workers.
ww.Sharing all PHI with anyone who asks, fo: Sharing all PHI with anyone who asks is the opposite of the standard. HIPAA requires limiting use and disclosure to what is needed, to protect patient privacy from needless exposure.
ww.The minimum number of nurses on each war: Staffing levels per ward are a nursing and management matter. The minimum necessary standard concerns how much protected health information may be used or shared, not how many nurses are on duty.

rw: A business associate agreement is a contract that requires a vendor handling PHI for a covered entity to protect it as HIPAA requires, with safeguards and limits on use and disclosure.

ww.A contract to rent space for a clinic in: Renting clinic space is a lease. A business associate agreement concerns vendors that handle protected health information, so a contract about renting a building does not match the term.
ww.A contract to hire staff for the wards a: Hiring staff for the wards is an employment contract. A BAA binds an outside vendor that handles protected health information, so a one year staffing contract is not what the term means.
ww.A contract to sell a business to a buyer: Selling a business to a buyer is a sale agreement. A business associate agreement is about protecting patient information held by vendors, so it does not transfer ownership of a business.

rw: Schedule I holds drugs with no accepted medical use and a high potential for abuse, such as heroin, so it is the most restricted of the controlled substance schedules and the correct answer.

ww.Schedule IV: Schedule IV drugs have a low potential for abuse and an accepted medical use. Drugs with no accepted medical use and high abuse potential are in Schedule I, not this one.
ww.Schedule V: Schedule V drugs have the lowest abuse potential among controlled drugs and accepted medical uses. The schedule with no accepted use and high abuse potential is Schedule I instead.
ww.Schedule III: Schedule III drugs have an accepted medical use and moderate to low potential for abuse. The category with no accepted medical use and high abuse potential is Schedule I.

rw: The DEA, or Drug Enforcement Administration, enforces controlled-substance laws and registers prescribers who can write prescriptions for controlled drugs, which links it directly to healthcare practice.

ww.Inspects food served in the cafeteria of: Inspecting cafeteria food is done by health departments and food safety inspectors. The DEA enforces controlled substance laws, so food inspection is not part of its work in healthcare.
ww.Licenses nurses who pass an exam and mee: Licensing nurses is done by state boards of nursing after an exam. The DEA is a federal agency for controlled substances and does not license nurses in general.
ww.Sets insurance rates charged to members: Setting insurance rates is done by insurers and state regulators. The DEA deals with controlled substances, so it has no role in the rates charged to members of a health plan.

rw: The FDA regulates the safety and effectiveness of drugs, medical devices and food, approving products before they reach the public and monitoring problems after, so this option correctly describes its role.

ww.Hospital billing and the claims sent to: Billing and claims sent to insurers are handled by payers and by agencies such as CMS. The FDA regulates drugs, devices and food, so it does not oversee hospital billing.
ww.Nurse staffing levels for each ward in t: Nurse staffing levels are set by hospital policy and some state rules. The FDA regulates drugs, devices and food, and does not decide how many nurses work on each ward.
ww.Insurance premiums charged to members of: Insurance premiums are regulated by state insurance departments and by health plan rules. The FDA regulates the safety of drugs, devices and food, and has no role in premium prices.

rw: State medical boards license physicians to practice in the state and discipline those who break standards, which protects the public by keeping unfit or unsafe doctors from treating patients.

ww.Billing insurers for the care given: Billing insurers is done by providers and billing offices. State medical boards license and discipline physicians, so they do not handle claims for the care given.
ww.Setting drug prices for pharmacies: Setting drug prices is not the job of state medical boards. They license and discipline physicians, while prices result from manufacturers, insurers and the market.
ww.Building hospitals in the whole state: Building hospitals is done by owners, developers and health systems. State medical boards focus on licensing and disciplining physicians, so construction across a state is not their function.

rw: The National Practitioner Data Bank is a federal database that tracks malpractice payments and certain adverse actions against practitioners, so hospitals and boards can review a clinician's history before granting privileges.

ww.A data bank of recipes that cooks and ch: A recipe database for kitchens is not a healthcare data bank. The National Practitioner Data Bank is a federal database about practitioners, malpractice payments and adverse actions, not food planning.
ww.A blood bank that stores units of blood: A blood bank stores blood for transfusions. The National Practitioner Data Bank stores information about practitioners and malpractice, not blood, even though both use the word bank in the name.
ww.A bank for money where hospitals keep th: A bank that keeps money and lends funds is a financial institution. The National Practitioner Data Bank holds information on practitioners and adverse actions, not hospital funds or loans.

rw: A Good Samaritan law protects people who give reasonable emergency help from liability, which encourages bystanders and off-duty professionals to assist at an emergency without fear of being sued if things go wrong.

ww.A law on hospital beds that sets how man: Hospital bed limits are set by licensing and capacity rules. A Good Samaritan law protects people who give emergency help, so it does not set how many beds a ward may hold.
ww.A law that punishes helpers who give car: A Good Samaritan law does the opposite of punishing helpers. It protects people who give reasonable emergency help from liability, so that bystanders are not discouraged from aiding a stranger.
ww.A law on charity taxes that sets what ho: Charity taxes are a tax law matter. A Good Samaritan law concerns liability protection for emergency helpers, and does not set what hospitals pay on gifts they receive.

rw: Vicarious liability is an employer's responsibility for the acts of employees done within the scope of their work, so a hospital can be held liable for a nurse's negligence on duty.

ww.A patient's liability for care that was: A patient's duty to pay for care is a financial obligation. Vicarious liability concerns an employer being responsible for what employees do at work, not what a patient owes.
ww.An employee's liability for the employer: An employee paying an employer's debts is not vicarious liability. The doctrine runs the other way, with the employer answering for employees' acts done within the scope of their work.
ww.A liability for lost items such as coats: Lost items such as coats and keys fall under bailment or property loss. Vicarious liability is about responsibility for the acts of others, not a duty for belongings left behind.

rw: A statute of limitations is the time limit within which a malpractice claim must be filed, and after it passes the claim is generally barred, however strong the case might have been.

ww.A limit on damages only, set by the cour: A limit on damages only is a damages cap. A statute of limitations sets a deadline for filing a claim, not a ceiling on what the court may award.
ww.A limit on staff numbers in each ward of: A limit on staff numbers per ward is a staffing rule. A statute of limitations in a malpractice case is about time, not about how many people work in a ward.
ww.A limit on the patients a doctor may tre: Limiting the patients a doctor treats in a week is a workload rule. A statute of limitations is a filing deadline, and has nothing to do with how many patients are seen.

rw: Capacity is the clinical ability to make a specific decision at a given time, assessed by clinicians, while competence is a legal determination made by a court, so the two are related but different.

ww.Capacity is legal, while competence is a: This reverses the terms. Capacity is the clinical ability to make a specific decision, judged by clinicians, while competence is a legal determination made by a court, so the option mislabels both.
ww.Neither matters in care, since doctors d: Capacity matters greatly in care, because consent must come from someone able to decide. Doctors cannot simply do whatever a patient wants if the patient lacks the ability to understand the choices.
ww.They are exactly the same thing, so a do: The terms are not the same. Capacity is a clinical judgment about one decision and competence is a legal status set by a court, so a doctor's view alone does not settle competence.

rw: When a patient lacks capacity and has no advance directive, a legally authorized surrogate, often a family member, usually makes decisions based on the patient's known wishes or best interests.

ww.A stranger who happens to be near the pa: A stranger nearby has no legal authority to decide for the patient. Decisions go to a legally authorized surrogate such as a family member, chosen under the law and not by chance.
ww.The insurer that pays the claims for the: An insurer pays claims and has no authority to make treatment decisions for the patient. A legally authorized surrogate, often a family member, decides when the patient lacks capacity.
ww.The nearest hospital employee on duty at: The nearest hospital employee on duty has no legal authority to consent for the patient. A legally authorized surrogate, often a family member, is the usual decision maker in this case.

rw: A living will is a document stating a person's wishes about medical treatment if they can no longer speak for themselves, such as whether to use life support, which guides doctors and family.

ww.A will that gives away property to heirs: A will that gives property to heirs after death is a last will and testament. A living will is about medical treatment wishes while the person is alive but unable to speak for themselves.
ww.A will for living things such as plants: Plants and pets need care, but a living will has nothing to do with living things in that sense. It records the person's own wishes about medical treatment if they cannot speak for themselves.
ww.A will written after death by the heirs: Heirs cannot write a will after a person dies, and sharing out an estate is handled by a last will. A living will records the person's treatment wishes while still alive.

rw: A POLST form is a medical order that records a seriously ill patient's treatment wishes, such as resuscitation or breathing support, so other clinicians and emergency staff can honor them across settings.

ww.A form for parking that lets staff and v: Parking forms are a facilities matter. POLST stands for Provider Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment and is a medical order, so a form to reserve spaces near the entrance is wrong.
ww.A form for hiring that lists the skills: A hiring form lists skills and pay and belongs to human resources. A POLST form is a medical order about life-sustaining treatment, so it has nothing to do with new staff.
ww.A form for billing that lists the charge: A billing form lists charges for services. A POLST form is a medical order about treatment wishes, so it is a clinical document rather than a record of charges to a patient.

rw: Brady- means slow, as in bradycardia, a slow heart rate. The prefix is used in terms that describe a reduced speed or rate, which is the opposite of fast.

ww.Fast: Fast is the meaning of tachy-, as in tachycardia, a fast heart rate. Brady- is the opposite prefix and means slow, as in bradycardia, so this option reverses the two.
ww.Large: Large is the meaning of macro- or mega-, as in megacolon. Brady- means slow, so large does not match the prefix used in bradycardia.
ww.Small: Small is the meaning of micro-, as in microscope. Brady- means slow, as in bradycardia, so small does not match the prefix in the question.

rw: Tachy- means fast, as in tachycardia, which is a fast heart rate. The prefix describes an increased speed or rate, and this is the standard meaning in medical terminology.

ww.Across: Across is the meaning of trans- or dia-, as in transfusion. Tachy- means fast, so across is the wrong meaning for the prefix in tachycardia.
ww.Slow: Slow is the meaning of brady-, as in bradycardia. Tachy- is its opposite and means fast, so this option gives the meaning of the other prefix.
ww.Below: Below is the meaning of sub- or hypo-, as in subcutaneous or hypodermic. Tachy- means fast, so below is not the meaning of this prefix.

rw: The suffix -emia means a condition of the blood, as in anemia or leukemia, where the word ending tells that the term refers to something found in the blood.

ww.Inflammation of a body part: Inflammation of a body part is the suffix -itis, as in arthritis. The suffix -emia refers to a condition of the blood, as in anemia, so this option gives the wrong suffix.
ww.Removal of a body part: Removal of a body part is the suffix -ectomy, as in appendectomy. The suffix -emia refers to a blood condition, so removal does not match this ending.
ww.Pain in a body part or nerve: Pain in a body part or nerve is the suffix -algia or -dynia, as in neuralgia. The suffix -emia refers to the blood, so pain does not fit.

rw: The suffix -algia means pain, as in neuralgia, which is nerve pain, and myalgia, which is muscle pain, so the ending marks a painful condition in a body part.

ww.Removal: Removal is the meaning of -ectomy, as in appendectomy. The suffix -algia means pain, as in neuralgia, so this option gives the meaning of a different surgical suffix.
ww.Swelling: Swelling is related to terms like edema. The suffix -algia means pain, as in neuralgia, so swelling does not match this ending in medical terms.
ww.Study of: Study of is the meaning of -ology, as in cardiology. The suffix -algia means pain, so a study or science does not match this ending.

rw: The suffix -plasty means surgical repair or reconstruction, as in rhinoplasty, which reshapes the nose, so the ending signals that a body part is being rebuilt or reshaped by a surgeon.

ww.Surgical removal of a body part: Surgical removal of a body part is the suffix -ectomy, as in appendectomy. The suffix -plasty means surgical repair or reconstruction, so removal is the wrong meaning here.
ww.Cutting into a vein or artery: Cutting into a vein or artery is not a suffix meaning. The suffix -plasty means surgical repair or reconstruction, and cutting into a body part would be -otomy.
ww.Viewing the inside of the body: Viewing the inside of the body is the suffix -scopy, as in endoscopy. The suffix -plasty means surgical repair or reconstruction, so viewing is not its meaning.

rw: The suffix -scopy means visual examination with an instrument, as in endoscopy or colonoscopy, where a scope lets the clinician see inside the body without a large incision.

ww.Inflammation of a joint or a body part: Inflammation of a joint or a body part is the suffix -itis, as in arthritis. The suffix -scopy means visual examination with an instrument, so inflammation does not match this ending.
ww.Surgical repair of a body part now: Surgical repair of a body part is the suffix -plasty, as in rhinoplasty. The suffix -scopy means looking with an instrument, so repair is the wrong meaning for this ending.
ww.Surgical removal of a part of the body: Surgical removal of a part is the suffix -ectomy, as in appendectomy. The suffix -scopy means visual examination with an instrument, so removal does not fit this ending.

rw: The suffix -otomy means a cutting into a body part, as in tracheotomy, where an opening is cut into the windpipe, and the part is not removed or repaired.

ww.Removal of a part: Removal of a part is the suffix -ectomy, as in appendectomy. The suffix -otomy means a cutting into, so this option gives the meaning of a different surgical suffix.
ww.Study of cells: Study of cells is cytology, from the root cyto- and the suffix -ology. The suffix -otomy means a cutting into, so study of cells does not match this ending.
ww.Repair of a part: Repair of a part is the suffix -plasty, as in rhinoplasty. The suffix -otomy means a cutting into, so repair is not the meaning of this ending.

rw: The root pulmon refers to the lung, as in pulmonary, which describes things related to the lungs, such as a pulmonary embolism or pulmonary function tests.

ww.Liver: Liver is hepat-, as in hepatitis. The root pulmon refers to the lung, as in pulmonary, so the liver is the wrong organ for this root.
ww.Heart: Heart is cardi-, as in cardiology. The root pulmon refers to the lung, as in pulmonary, so the heart is the wrong organ for this root.
ww.Kidney: Kidney is ren- or nephr-, as in renal or nephritis. The root pulmon refers to the lung, as in pulmonary, so the kidney is the wrong organ here.

rw: The roots hem and hemat refer to blood, as in hematology, the study of blood, and hemorrhage, which is bleeding, so these roots mark terms about blood.

ww.Skin: Skin is derm- or dermat-, as in dermatitis. The roots hem and hemat refer to blood, as in hematology, so skin is the wrong body part.
ww.Bone: Bone is oste-, as in osteoporosis. The roots hem and hemat refer to blood, as in hematology, so bone does not match these roots.
ww.Liver: Liver is hepat-, as in hepatitis. The roots hem and hemat refer to blood, as in hematology, so liver is not the meaning of these roots.

rw: The root my refers to muscle, as in myalgia, which is muscle pain, and myocardium, the heart muscle, so this root marks terms about muscle tissue.

ww.Nerve: Nerve is neur- or neuro-, as in neurology. The root my refers to muscle, as in myalgia, so nerve is the wrong tissue for this root.
ww.Skin: Skin is derm- or dermat-, as in dermatitis. The root my refers to muscle, as in myalgia, so skin is the wrong meaning for this root.
ww.Bone: Bone is oste-, as in osteoporosis. The root my refers to muscle, as in myalgia, so bone does not match this root in medical terms.

rw: The root arthr refers to a joint, as in arthritis, which is inflammation of a joint, and arthroscopy, which is a look inside a joint with a scope.

ww.Muscle: Muscle is my- or myo-, as in myalgia. The root arthr refers to a joint, as in arthritis, so muscle is the wrong tissue for this root.
ww.Bone: Bone is oste-, as in osteoporosis. The root arthr refers to a joint, as in arthritis, where bones meet, so bone is not the meaning of this root.
ww.Skin: Skin is derm- or dermat-, as in dermatitis. The root arthr refers to a joint, as in arthritis, so skin is the wrong body part here.

rw: The root ophthalm refers to the eye, as in ophthalmology, the study of the eye and its diseases, and ophthalmoscope, an instrument used to look into the eye.

ww.Ear: Ear is ot- or aur-, as in otitis. The root ophthalm refers to the eye, as in ophthalmology, so the ear is the wrong organ for this root.
ww.Nose: Nose is rhin-, as in rhinoplasty. The root ophthalm refers to the eye, as in ophthalmology, so the nose is not the meaning of this root.
ww.Skin: Skin is derm- or dermat-, as in dermatitis. The root ophthalm refers to the eye, as in ophthalmology, so skin is the wrong body part here.

rw: The root ot refers to the ear, as in otitis, an inflammation of the ear, and otology, the study of the ear, so this root marks terms about hearing and the ear.

ww.Eye: Eye is ophthalm- or opt-, as in ophthalmology. The root ot refers to the ear, as in otitis, so the eye is the wrong organ for this root.
ww.Throat: Throat is pharyng- or laryng-, as in pharyngitis. The root ot refers to the ear, as in otitis media, so throat is not the meaning of this root.
ww.Nose: Nose is rhin-, as in rhinitis. The root ot refers to the ear, as in otitis, so the nose is the wrong organ for this root.

rw: The root rhin refers to the nose, as in rhinitis, which is inflammation of the nasal lining, and rhinoplasty, which is surgical reshaping of the nose.

ww.Ear: Ear is ot- or aur-, as in otitis. The root rhin refers to the nose, as in rhinitis or rhinoplasty, so the ear is the wrong organ for this root.
ww.Eye: Eye is ophthalm- or opt-, as in ophthalmology. The root rhin refers to the nose, as in rhinitis, so the eye is not the meaning of this root.
ww.Mouth: Mouth is or- or stomat-, as in oral or stomatitis. The root rhin refers to the nose, as in rhinitis, so the mouth is the wrong part here.

rw: QID stands for quater in die, which means four times a day. It is used on prescriptions to tell the patient how often to take a dose, so this option is correct.

ww.Once a day only: Once a day is written as QD or daily, not QID. QID means four times a day, so a once daily dose would be four times too small.
ww.Twice a day only: Twice a day is written as BID. QID means four times a day, so this option gives only half the doses that the abbreviation QID calls for.
ww.Three times a day: Three times a day is written as TID. QID means four times a day, so a TID dose gives one fewer dose a day than QID requires.

rw: AC stands for ante cibum, which means before meals, so a drug marked AC is taken before eating, such as thirty minutes ahead, in order to work properly.

ww.As needed: As needed is PRN. The abbreviation AC means before meals, from the Latin ante cibum, so as needed is the wrong meaning for AC in a medication order.
ww.After meals: After meals is PC, from post cibum. The abbreviation AC means before meals, from ante cibum, so this option gives the opposite timing to what AC says.
ww.At bedtime: At bedtime is HS. The abbreviation AC means before meals, so a drug given at bedtime would be given at the wrong time if it is ordered AC.

rw: PC stands for post cibum, which means after meals, so a medication marked PC is taken after eating, often to lessen stomach upset or to match how food affects the drug.

ww.At bedtime: At bedtime is HS, from hora somni. The abbreviation PC means after meals, from post cibum, so bedtime is the wrong meaning for PC in a medication order.
ww.As needed: As needed is PRN. The abbreviation PC means after meals, from post cibum, so as needed does not match PC on a medication order.
ww.Before meals: Before meals is AC, from ante cibum. The abbreviation PC means after meals, from post cibum, so this option gives the opposite of what PC says.

rw: HS stands for hora somni, which means at bedtime, so a drug marked HS is given at the hour of sleep, such as a sleep aid or a drug best taken before resting.

ww.Before meals: Before meals is AC, from ante cibum. The abbreviation HS means at bedtime, from hora somni, so before meals is the wrong meaning for HS on an order.
ww.After meals: After meals is PC, from post cibum. The abbreviation HS means at bedtime, so this option gives the meaning of a different abbreviation on a medication order.
ww.Every hour: Every hour is written as q1h or QH. The abbreviation HS means at bedtime, so an hourly schedule would be a far shorter interval than HS orders.

rw: PO stands for per os, which means by mouth, so a drug marked PO is swallowed as a tablet, capsule or liquid and taken by the oral route.

ww.Into the eye: Into the eye is an ophthalmic route, shown as OU, OD or OS for the eyes. PO means by mouth, so a drug into the eye would be a wrong route.
ww.By injection: By injection is a parenteral route such as IM, IV or SC. PO means by mouth, so an injection is the wrong route for a drug ordered PO.
ww.Under tongue: Under the tongue is the sublingual route, written SL. PO means by mouth, to be swallowed, so a drug ordered PO is not meant to dissolve under the tongue.

rw: IV stands for intravenous, which means into a vein, so a drug or fluid given IV enters the bloodstream directly and acts quickly.

ww.By mouth, to be swallowed: By mouth, to be swallowed, is PO, from per os. IV means intravenous, into a vein, so a drug given by mouth is a different route from IV.
ww.Intramuscular, into muscle: Intramuscular, into muscle, is IM. IV means intravenous, into a vein, so this option gives the meaning of a different abbreviation for another injection route.
ww.Under the skin of a patient: Under the skin is subcutaneous, written SC or SQ. IV means intravenous, into a vein, so a drug given under the skin uses a different route than IV.

rw: IM stands for intramuscular, which means into a muscle, so a drug marked IM is given by injection deep into muscle tissue, where it is absorbed at a steady pace.

ww.By mouth, to be swallowed: By mouth, to be swallowed, is PO. IM means intramuscular, into a muscle, so a drug given by mouth is a different route from the injection that IM describes.
ww.Under the tongue, to dissolve: Under the tongue, to dissolve, is the sublingual route, written SL. IM means intramuscular, into a muscle, so this option gives the meaning of another route.
ww.Intravenous, into a vein: Intravenous, into a vein, is IV. IM means intramuscular, into a muscle, so a drug given into a vein is the wrong route for IM.

rw: CBC stands for complete blood count, a common lab test that measures red cells, white cells and platelets in a blood sample to check health and find conditions such as infection or anemia.

ww.Chronic bone condition: Chronic bone condition is not what CBC stands for. A CBC is a blood test, so a term naming a bone problem does not match the lab abbreviation.
ww.Central brain center: Central brain center is not a medical term used for CBC. The abbreviation CBC stands for complete blood count, a common blood test, and not an organ of the brain.
ww.Cardiac blood circuit: Cardiac blood circuit is not the meaning of CBC. The abbreviation stands for complete blood count, a lab test of blood cells, and not a path of blood through the heart.

rw: An ECG or EKG records the electrical activity of the heart, shown as a tracing, which helps clinicians find rhythm problems, heart attacks and other heart conditions.

ww.Muscle strength of the patient's arm: Muscle strength of the arm is not recorded by an ECG. Strength is tested by physical examination, while an ECG records electrical activity of the heart rather than a limb.
ww.Lung capacity of a patient at rest: Lung capacity at rest is measured by spirometry or pulmonary function tests. An ECG records the electrical activity of the heart, so it does not measure breathing volume.
ww.Brain waves of a patient when asleep: Brain waves during sleep are recorded by an EEG. An ECG or EKG records the electrical activity of the heart, so it does not show brain waves.

rw: An EEG, or electroencephalogram, records the electrical activity of the brain, shown as waves on a tracing, and it helps diagnose seizures, sleep problems and other brain conditions.

ww.The electrical activity of the heart: The electrical activity of the heart is recorded by an ECG or EKG. An EEG records the brain, so this option gives the test for the wrong organ.
ww.The electrical activity of the muscles: The electrical activity of muscles is recorded by an EMG, or electromyogram. An EEG records the brain, so muscle activity is not what this test shows.
ww.The electrical activity of the lungs: The lungs are tested with pulmonary function tests and imaging, not electrical recordings. An EEG records the electrical activity of the brain, so lung activity is not its subject.

rw: MRI stands for magnetic resonance imaging, a scan that uses strong magnets and radio waves to make detailed pictures of soft tissues, organs and joints without using radiation.

ww.Muscle repair injection: Muscle repair injection is not a real expansion of MRI. MRI is an imaging scan and does not repair muscle or involve any injection to treat it.
ww.Major risk inventory list: Major risk inventory list is not a medical term. MRI stands for magnetic resonance imaging, a type of scan, and not a list of risks kept by an organization.
ww.Medical records index file: Medical records index file is a made up phrase. MRI means magnetic resonance imaging, a scan that takes pictures inside the body, and it is not a records system.

rw: CT stands for computed tomography, an imaging method that uses X-rays and a computer to make cross-sectional pictures of the body, which show organs, bones and other tissues in detail.

ww.Cardiac test result: Cardiac test result is not what CT stands for in imaging. CT means computed tomography, a scan, and the letters do not name a test result of the heart.
ww.Clinical trial of drugs: Clinical trial of drugs is a research study, not an imaging term. In imaging, CT means computed tomography, a scan, so this option gives an unrelated phrase from research.
ww.Chest tube drain: Chest tube drain is a treatment device and not an imaging term. In imaging, CT stands for computed tomography, a scan that makes cross-sectional pictures of the body.

rw: A chief complaint is the main reason a patient seeks care, recorded in the patient's own words, such as chest pain for two days, and it guides the rest of the visit.

ww.A complaint about billing made by a pati: A complaint about billing is a patient grievance sent to the billing office. A chief complaint is the main reason for the visit recorded at the start of an encounter.
ww.A complaint by a manager about a member: A complaint by a manager about staff is a personnel issue handled by human resources. A chief complaint is the patient's main reason for seeking care, so this option is unrelated.
ww.A complaint about the hospital made by a: A complaint about the hospital made to a manager is a grievance. A chief complaint is the main reason the patient seeks care, recorded in the patient's own words.

rw: In a SOAP note, the A stands for assessment, which is the clinician's evaluation or diagnosis based on the subjective and objective information gathered in the visit.

ww.Allergy: Allergy is recorded in the history, but it is not what the A in SOAP stands for. SOAP means subjective, objective, assessment and plan, so A is assessment.
ww.Admission: Admission is a stage of a hospital stay, not a part of a SOAP note. The A in SOAP stands for assessment, the clinician's diagnosis or impression after reviewing the findings.
ww.Action: Action is not a part of the SOAP format. SOAP stands for subjective, objective, assessment and plan, so the A is assessment, and the steps to take belong to the plan.

rw: In a SOAP note, the P stands for plan, which lists the treatment, tests, medications and follow up the clinician intends, based on the assessment of the patient's condition.

ww.Payment: Payment is not part of the SOAP note. SOAP stands for subjective, objective, assessment and plan, so the P is plan, and billing details are recorded elsewhere in the chart.
ww.Patient: Patient is not what the P stands for. The SOAP note is already about a patient, and the P means plan, the steps for treatment and follow up.
ww.Pulse: Pulse is a vital sign recorded under the objective part of the note. In SOAP, the P stands for plan, so pulse is not the meaning of the letter.

rw: A release of information form authorizes the sharing of a patient's records with a named person or organization, which respects privacy law by requiring the patient's permission before disclosure.

ww.To release a bill to the insurer or the: Releasing a bill is a billing task. A release of information form authorizes sharing a patient's records, so it is not used to send a bill to an insurer.
ww.To release a patient from the hospital o: Discharging a patient from the hospital is done by a physician's order. An ROI form authorizes sharing records and does not release a patient from care at the hospital.
ww.To release staff from work early when th: Releasing staff from work early is a scheduling decision by managers. A release of information form concerns patient records, and has nothing to do with the hours that staff work.

rw: A master patient index is a database that links each patient to a unique identifier across a health system, so records for the same person can be found and matched correctly.

ww.A list of drugs kept by the pharmacy for: A list of drugs kept by the pharmacy is a formulary or inventory. A master patient index links each patient to a unique identifier, so it is not a drug list.
ww.A list of staff kept by the office for e: A list of staff kept by the office is a staff directory. A master patient index is a database of patients and their identifiers, so it is not a list of employees.
ww.A list of beds kept by the ward for each: A list of beds is a bed census or room inventory. A master patient index is a database of patients, so a list of beds in a building is the wrong thing.

rw: A duplicate record splits a patient's information across two charts, so a clinician may miss allergies, medications or history, and incomplete information could harm the patient, which is why duplicates are a safety problem.

ww.Lower costs only, with no effect on care: A duplicate record does not only lower costs. It adds cost through rework and risks harm to patients, so claiming no effect on care quality is incorrect.
ww.Faster care for all patients seen in the: Duplicate records slow care rather than speed it. Staff must search and reconcile several charts, and missing information can delay or harm treatment, so faster care for patients is not the result.
ww.Better privacy for the records of each p: Duplicate records do not improve privacy. They can lead to information being sent to the wrong place or being missed, and they make it harder to protect the records of each patient.

rw: A patient registration form collects demographic, contact and insurance information, which identifies the patient, allows the office to reach them and supports billing and claims for the visit.

ww.To collect donations only, from patients: Collecting donations is not the purpose of a registration form. It gathers the information needed to identify and treat the patient and to bill, and donations are handled by other channels.
ww.To advertise the clinic to people who li: Advertising the clinic is a marketing task. A registration form collects information from the patient for the record, not a message sent to people who live in the town.
ww.To list staff birthdays and the dates of: Staff birthdays and anniversaries are human resources information. A patient registration form is completed by patients and collects demographic, contact and insurance details, not facts about employees.

rw: Collecting the co-pay at the time of service is the best practice, because the patient is present, the amount is known and the office avoids later billing costs and unpaid balances.

ww.Ignore it until the bill is due: Ignoring a co-pay until the bill is due is poor practice, because it delays payment and makes collection harder. The best practice is to collect it at the time of service.
ww.Wait six months to bill the patient: Waiting six months to bill the patient delays revenue and makes collection less likely. A co-pay should be collected at check-in, at the time of service, as the best practice.
ww.Collect it by mail only, later on: Collecting only by mail later delays payment and adds billing costs and the risk of nonpayment. The best practice is to collect the co-pay at the time of service.

rw: A wait-time statistic measures how long patients wait to be seen, from arrival or appointment time until care begins, and it helps a clinic judge access and patient satisfaction.

ww.How long staff wait for breaks: How long staff wait for breaks is a staffing matter. A wait-time statistic measures how long patients wait to be seen, so staff break times are not what it tracks.
ww.How long a drug takes to work: How long a drug takes to work is a pharmacology measure. A wait-time statistic measures how long patients wait to be seen, so drug action time is not part of it.
ww.How long an operation lasts there: How long an operation lasts is a surgical duration measure. A wait-time statistic measures how long patients wait to be seen, not the length of a procedure.

rw: Appointment reminders reduce no-shows, the visits that patients miss without notice, by prompting patients by phone, text or mail, which fills the schedule better and improves access to care.

ww.Staff pay: Reminders do not reduce staff pay. They are a scheduling tool that lowers missed visits, and pay is set by employment terms, so this option has no link to what reminders do.
ww.Coverage: Reminders do not reduce insurance coverage. Coverage is set by the health plan, and reminders only prompt patients to attend visits, so the two are unrelated.
ww.Safety: Reminders do not reduce safety. They help patients keep appointments and receive care on time, which supports safe care, so the idea that they reduce safety is the reverse of their effect.

rw: A walk-in appointment is a visit without a scheduled time, where the patient arrives and is seen as the clinic can fit them in, rather than at a time booked ahead.

ww.A visit on foot by a patient: A visit on foot describes how a patient arrives, not the type of appointment. A walk-in appointment is defined by having no scheduled time, not by how the patient travels.
ww.A visit by video call only here: A video call is a telehealth visit. A walk-in appointment is an in-person visit without a scheduled time, so a visit by video call only is a different type of visit.
ww.A visit by mail or by post only: A visit by mail or post is not an appointment. A walk-in appointment is an in-person visit without a scheduled time, so mail is unrelated to what a walk-in means.

rw: Wave scheduling books several patients at the start of each hour and sees them in order of arrival, which allows for late arrivals and no-shows and keeps the provider busy throughout the hour.

ww.Scheduling by phone only, with no visits: Phone only scheduling describes a booking channel. Wave scheduling is about booking several patients at the start of each hour, so limiting booking to the phone does not define it.
ww.Booking one patient a day and no more, w: Booking one patient a day is far too slow for a clinic and is not wave scheduling. Wave scheduling books several patients at the start of each hour, so it is the opposite.
ww.Scheduling at the beach, so that visits: Scheduling at the beach is not a real scheduling method. Wave scheduling books several patients at the start of each hour, and the word wave has nothing to do with the sea.

rw: Open-access scheduling keeps slots open so patients can be seen the day they call, which reduces waiting and no-shows, and gives patients quick access to care when they need it.

ww.Booking months ahead only, with no slots: Booking months ahead only is the opposite of open access. Open access scheduling keeps slots free so patients can be seen the same day they call, not months later.
ww.Leaving the office doors open so patient: Leaving the doors open for walk-ins at any hour is not what open access means. It is a scheduling method that holds appointment slots for same-day calls, and not an unlimited walk-in policy.
ww.Booking only new patients and turning aw: Booking only new patients and turning away others is not open access. The method keeps slots free so any patient who calls can be seen the same day, including existing patients.

rw: The best way is to follow clinic policy, seeing the patient if the schedule allows or rescheduling politely, which keeps the office fair to others and treats the late patient with respect.

ww.Scold them in front of the other patient: Scolding a patient in front of others is unprofessional and harms trust. A late patient should be treated with courtesy while the clinic follows its own policy on late arrivals.
ww.Refuse to speak to them and ask them to: Refusing to speak to the patient and asking them to leave is rude and ignores clinic policy. The staff should follow policy, either seeing the patient if possible or rescheduling politely.
ww.Ignore them and carry on with the work o: Ignoring the patient is unprofessional and leaves them unsure about their care. Staff should greet them and follow clinic policy, either seeing them if possible or rescheduling in a polite way.

rw: Scarcity means limited resources to meet unlimited wants, so people and societies must make choices about how to use what they have, which is the central problem of economics.

ww.A tax placed on rare goods and on gems: A tax on rare goods and gems is a luxury tax or tariff. Scarcity is the basic problem of limited resources to meet unlimited wants, and not a tax on any item.
ww.A shortage of money in one family or hom: A shortage of money in one family is a personal budget problem. Scarcity is the economic problem that all resources are limited compared with unlimited wants, and it applies to every society.
ww.Having more goods than anyone can use: Having more goods than anyone can use is a surplus, which is the opposite of scarcity. Scarcity means that resources are limited compared with the wants people have.

rw: A need is something required to live, such as food and shelter, which people cannot go without, and this separates needs from wants, which people can live without for a long time.

ww.Something you like but can live without: Something you like but can live without is a want. A need is something required to live, such as food and shelter, so this option describes a want instead.
ww.Something advertised on television and i: Something advertised on television is just a product that is marketed. Advertising does not make something a need, since a need is something required to live, such as food and shelter.
ww.Something that costs a lot of money to b: Something that costs a lot of money may be a luxury, not a need. A need is something required to live, such as food and shelter, whatever its price might be.

rw: A want is something you desire that is not essential for survival, such as a game or a new phone, so people can live without it while still wishing to have it.

ww.Something required for health, such as f: Something required for health, such as food and shelter, is a need. A want is something you desire but is not essential for survival, so this describes the opposite.
ww.Something the law requires you to buy ea: Something the law requires you to buy each year is an obligation, such as insurance in some places. A want is something desired that is not essential for survival.
ww.Something that cannot be bought with mon: Many wants can be bought with money, such as toys and entertainment. A want is something desired but not essential for survival, so saying it can never be bought is wrong.

rw: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best choice you give up when you make a decision, so every choice has a cost measured by the best alternative left behind.

ww.The cost of making a product in a factor: The cost of making a product in a factory is a production cost. Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up, not the money spent making goods.
ww.The price you pay at the store, with the: The price at the store with tax is the money cost of an item. Opportunity cost is the value of the next best choice you give up, which may not be a money price.
ww.The tax added at checkout on a purchase: The tax added at checkout is a sales tax. Opportunity cost is the value of the next best choice you give up, so a tax on a purchase is a different idea.

rw: Jamal's opportunity cost of going to the concert is the $60 he could have earned by working, because that is the value of the next best alternative that he gives up.

ww.Nothing, as the concert is free: The concert is free, but going still has a cost. Jamal gives up the chance to earn $60, so his opportunity cost is the $60 and not nothing.
ww.The cost of the concert ticket: There is no ticket cost, because the concert is free. Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative given up, which here is $60 in wages, not a ticket price.
ww.The cost of a snack he buys: A snack is an extra expense, not the next best choice he gives up by going. His opportunity cost is the $60 he could have earned working on Saturday instead.

rw: Goods are physical products that people buy, such as shoes, food and cars, which can be touched and owned, and this separates them from services, which are work done for others.

ww.Ideas that cannot be sold or traded at a: Ideas that cannot be sold or traded are not goods in economics. Goods are physical products that people buy, such as shoes, and they are things that can be bought and sold.
ww.Money earned from a job each week or mon: Money earned from a job is income, not a good. Goods are physical products that people buy, such as shoes, and income is what people use to buy them.
ww.Work done for someone else, such as a ha: Work done for someone else, such as a haircut, is a service. Goods are physical products that people buy, such as shoes, so this option describes the other category.

rw: Services are work performed for others, such as a haircut, a medical exam or a repair, where the buyer receives the benefit of labor and not a physical product to keep.

ww.Products that can be touched and held by: Products that can be touched and held are goods. Services are work performed for others, such as a haircut, so this option describes goods and gives the wrong category.
ww.Natural resources like land and water bo: Natural resources like land and water are factors of production. Services are work performed for others, such as a haircut, so this option describes a different idea in economics.
ww.Machines used in a factory to make goods: Machines used in a factory are capital, a factor of production. Services are work performed for others, such as a haircut, so machines are not the meaning of services.

rw: A dentist cleaning your teeth is a service, because it is work done for you by another person and gives you a benefit but not a physical product to take away.

ww.A loaf of bread from a shop: A loaf of bread is a physical product that can be held, so it is a good. A service is work done for others, so bread is not an example.
ww.A new bicycle from a store: A new bicycle is a physical product bought from a store, so it is a good. A service is work done for others, so a bicycle is not an example.
ww.A pair of running shoes bought: A pair of running shoes is a physical product that can be held and owned, so it is a good. A service is work done for others, so shoes are not an example.

rw: The four factors of production are land, labor, capital and entrepreneurship, the resources that are combined to make goods and services, and each one plays a distinct part in production.

ww.Banks, stores, farms and factories in to: Banks, stores, farms and factories are kinds of businesses and places. The four factors of production are land, labor, capital and entrepreneurship, which are the inputs businesses use, not the businesses themselves.
ww.Supply, demand, cost and revenue of firm: Supply, demand, cost and revenue are market concepts, not inputs to production. The four factors of production are land, labor, capital and entrepreneurship, which firms use to make goods and services.
ww.Price, profit, product and place of sale: Price, profit, product and place of sale are marketing and business terms. The four factors of production are land, labor, capital and entrepreneurship, which are the inputs for making goods.

rw: Labor as a factor of production is the physical and mental work people contribute to producing goods and services, such as a factory worker lifting parts or a designer planning a product.

ww.Tools and machines used in production at: Tools and machines used in production are capital, not labor. Labor is the physical and mental work people contribute to producing goods and services.
ww.The risk of starting a business for prof: The risk of starting a business is taken by an entrepreneur. Labor is the physical and mental work that people contribute, and it is a separate factor of production.
ww.Natural resources like water and soil in: Natural resources like water and soil are land, which is a different factor of production. Labor is the physical and mental work that people contribute to making goods and services.

rw: Capital as a factor of production means the tools, machines and buildings used to make goods, which are made by people and help workers produce more than they could by hand.

ww.Land and natural resources, such as fore: Land and natural resources, such as forests and rivers, are the factor called land. Capital is made up of tools, machines and buildings used to make goods, so this option describes land.
ww.The money in your wallet or in a bank ac: Money in a wallet or bank is financial capital in everyday speech, but it is not a factor of production. Capital in economics means tools, machines and buildings used to make goods.
ww.The work that people do to earn a wage e: The work people do to earn a wage is labor, a different factor of production. Capital in economics is made of tools, machines and buildings used to make goods and services.

rw: An entrepreneur starts a business and takes on its risks, organizing land, labor and capital in the hope of a profit, and also accepts that the venture may lose money.

ww.Lends money to the government for its ne: Lending money to the government is done by buyers of government bonds. An entrepreneur starts a business and takes on its risks, so lending for government needs is a different role.
ww.Works for a fixed wage at a factory each: Working for a fixed wage at a factory is the role of a worker, who supplies labor. An entrepreneur starts a business and takes on its risks, so a fixed wage does not fit.
ww.Collects taxes for the government each y: Collecting taxes for the government is done by tax agencies. An entrepreneur starts a business and takes on its risks, so collecting taxes is not what the role means.

rw: Demand is how much of a product buyers are willing and able to buy at a given price, and both willingness and ability to pay are needed for real demand.

ww.How much of a product sellers will offer: How much of a product sellers will offer at each price is supply, not demand. Demand is how much buyers are willing and able to buy at a price.
ww.The number of stores in a town or a city: The number of stores selling goods is a count of sellers in a market. Demand is how much of a product buyers are willing and able to buy at a price.
ww.The price a store sets for a good or ser: The price a store sets for a good is a price chosen by the seller. Demand describes how much buyers are willing and able to buy at a price, not the price set by a seller.

rw: Supply is how much of a product sellers are willing to offer at a price, and it usually rises when the price rises because selling more becomes more profitable for them.

ww.The profit earned on each item, the pric: The profit earned on each item, the price minus the cost, is profit per unit. Supply is how much sellers are willing to offer at a price, so profit is not its definition.
ww.The cost of materials used to make a goo: The cost of materials used to make a good is a production cost. Supply is how much sellers are willing to offer at a price, so a cost of materials does not define supply.
ww.How much buyers want to buy at a given p: How much buyers want to buy at a given price is demand, not supply. Supply is how much sellers are willing to offer at a price, so this option describes the buyers' side.

rw: The law of demand says that as price rises, buyers usually buy less, because a higher price makes a good cost more compared with other things the buyers could choose.

ww.As price rises, sellers must produce les: As price rises, sellers produce more, not less, which is the law of supply. The law of demand concerns buyers and says that a higher price usually leads to buying less.
ww.Price never affects buying by people: Price does affect buying, so the claim that it never does is wrong. The law of demand says that as price rises, buyers usually buy less of a good.
ww.As price rises, buyers usually buy more: As price rises, buyers usually buy less, not more. Buying more at a higher price would reverse the law of demand, which is an inverse link between price and quantity bought.

rw: The law of supply says that as price rises, sellers usually offer more of a good, because a higher price makes selling more profitable, which is a direct link between price and quantity supplied.

ww.Sellers ignore price completely when the: Sellers do respond to price, so ignoring it completely is wrong. The law of supply says that as price rises, sellers usually offer more of a good for sale.
ww.As price rises, sellers usually offer le: As price rises, sellers usually offer more, not less, because higher prices bring higher profits. Offering less at a higher price would reverse the law of supply.
ww.Buyers decide what sellers must then mak: The law of supply is about how sellers respond to price, not about buyers deciding what sellers make. It says that as price rises, sellers usually offer more.

rw: The equilibrium price is the price at which the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded, so there is no surplus or shortage and the market clears at that price.

ww.The lowest price allowed by law for good: The lowest price allowed by law is a price floor, such as a minimum wage. The equilibrium price is where the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded.
ww.The price set by a store manager for goo: A price set by a store manager is a chosen price and may not clear the market. The equilibrium price is where the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded.
ww.The highest price a seller can charge be: The highest price a seller can charge before buyers stop buying is not the equilibrium price. Equilibrium is where the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded, with no leftover goods or unmet demand.

rw: A surplus occurs when the quantity supplied is greater than the quantity demanded at the current price, as with a store that has more shirts than customers want to buy.

ww.A monopoly: A monopoly is a market with a single seller. A store with more shirts than customers want at the current price has a surplus, so monopoly is the wrong term.
ww.A shortage: A shortage is the opposite case, where customers want more than is available. More shirts than customers want at the current price is a surplus, so shortage is wrong.
ww.A balance: A balance would mean the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded, which is equilibrium. Here the store has more shirts than customers want, so there is a surplus.

rw: A shortage occurs when the quantity demanded is greater than the quantity supplied at the current price, as when customers want more concert tickets than are available.

ww.A tariff: A tariff is a tax on imported goods. Customers wanting more tickets than are available at the current price is a shortage, so a tariff is the wrong term.
ww.Equilibrium: Equilibrium is when the quantity supplied equals the quantity demanded. Here customers want more tickets than exist at the current price, so the market is not in equilibrium.
ww.A surplus: A surplus is when the quantity supplied is greater than the quantity demanded. Here customers want more tickets than are available, which is the opposite, so it is a shortage.

rw: Inflation is a general rise in prices over time, which means each unit of money buys less than before, so the cost of living goes up across the economy.

ww.A rise in the price of one item only: A rise in the price of one item only is a change in a relative price. Inflation is a general rise in prices across the economy over time.
ww.A rise in the number of workers: A rise in the number of workers is employment or labor force growth. Inflation is a general rise in prices over time, so the number of workers is unrelated.
ww.A general fall in prices over time: A general fall in prices over time is deflation, the opposite of inflation. Inflation is a general rise in prices over time, so this option reverses the meaning.
